e-7454.problem:
What is the area scale factor of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ that is given by its standard matrix 

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$
e-7454.worked_solution:
The area scale factor of a linear transformation $\mathbf T$ with standard matrix $T$ is equal to $|\det(T)|.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}|det(T)| & =|2\cdot 4-3\cdot 1| \\  & =|8-3| \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039564/assets/e8ff769df4089e6ed9a47d56d7317acf41b8aef6a255abc705c0e7ec31a446ea.png)

Consider the shaded region $D$ shown above. What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$
e-5470.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $\mathbf{T},$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $\mathbf{T}(D)$ under the action of $\mathbf{T}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\text{Area}(\mathbf{T}(D)) = |\det(T)| \cdot \text{Area}(D)
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D) = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \cdot 4 = 6.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
\det(T) = 4 \cdot 2 -  2 \cdot (-1) = 10.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,10\,|\cdot 6 \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$

e-5471.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of the Image of an Object Under a Linear Transformation
e-5471.problem:
A triangle $D$ has vertices $(1,1)$, $(4,5),$ and $(-2,1).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
[\begin{aligned}-7 & 5 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
e-5471.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039564/assets/ee8f0cf16983d87fa505303ed6372a3f389518d05b3e13f2e9e2121038792b84.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $\mathbf{T},$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $\mathbf{T}(D)$ under the action of $\mathbf{T}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\text{Area}(\mathbf{T}(D)) = |\det(T)| \cdot \text{Area}(D)
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D) = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \cdot 4 = 6.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
\det(T) = (-7) \cdot 3 -  5 \cdot (-2) = -11.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|-11|\cdot 6 \\  & =66.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039564/assets/455e0a08e2a0929a60d7fa1b76973e1b7a460efe8cc1cf01719ce211feacd8c0.png)

Consider the shaded region $D$ shown above. What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

$\text{Area}(T(D))=$
{{field-1}}
content.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 4=6.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=1\cdot 1-3\cdot 2=-5.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,-5\,|\cdot 6 \\  & =30.\end{aligned}
$$

A triangle $D$ has vertices $(-2,-1),(3,-1),(1,3).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039564/assets/10c831c616279f443d10ed478a8b3b173d598da6e9b0b45edb7ecf487cf97f92.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 5\cdot 4=10.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=2\cdot 3-1\cdot 0=6.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,6\,|\cdot 10 \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$
